title: Charcoal Briquettes 8kg

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday)
drivers.evidence: One day lost in a 7-day week. Historical data shows no consistent sales impact from partial closures. The baseline already reflects declining trend, so only a small downward adjustment is justified.

adjustment.analysis: The store closure on Monday (2026-10-19) removes one day of sales, reducing the week to 6 days. Historical data shows no significant effect from partial-week closures. The baseline already reflects seasonal decline (trend_13 vs prior_13: -32.2%). Halloween occurred last week (2026-10-12), and the product sold at 52% of baseline (noise-adjusted x0.68), which is already captured in the trend. No promotion or price change is active. The classical model's 0.68 is too low: it applies a one-time Halloween effect that's already baked into the downward trend. The 10% price increase is not applicable—price is unchanged. No evidence supports a demand lift. The median should be slightly adjusted down for the closure, but the noise-adjusted effect is negligible. The baseline uncertainty remains valid.

It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-73% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
